gui.simple_bytestorage.guide.title: Simple Byte Storage Guide
guide.simple_bytestorage.intro.title: Introduction
guide.simple_bytestorage.intro.body:
Simple Byte Storage stores items as bytes: §b1 item = 1 byte§r. There is no limit on the number of item types, only on total bytes.

§eHow to start§r
1. Place a §bNetwork Controller§r and power it (it accepts FE).
2. Put a §bDrive§r next to it and insert storage cells.
3. Place a §bTerminal§r next to it.

Blocks join the network simply by §btouching§r each other (or through Cables). Everything must connect to the controller, and the controller must be online.
guide.simple_bytestorage.network.title: Network & power
guide.simple_bytestorage.network.body:
§eController§r — the heart of the network. Buffer 100 000 FE, accepts up to 2 000 FE/t. Every device drains a little energy.

States: §aONLINE§r (works), §cOFFLINE§r (no power), §6CONFLICT§r (two controllers in one network).

§eCable§r — carries the network over distance. Devices also connect directly by touching.

The network is re-scanned every second, so changes take effect quickly.
guide.simple_bytestorage.storage.title: Drives & cells
guide.simple_bytestorage.storage.body:
§eDrive§r holds up to 10 storage cells; all of them merge into one virtual pool.

§eCells§r: 1k (1 024 B), 4k (4 096 B), 16k (16 384 B), 64k (65 536 B).

§eDrive settings§r
- §bPriority§r: higher priority fills first (Shift: ±10).
- §bWhitelist§r: only listed items are accepted (empty = any).

Use priority + whitelist to sort items into dedicated drives.
guide.simple_bytestorage.terminals.title: Terminals
guide.simple_bytestorage.terminals.body:
§eTerminal§r — browse and take items from the whole network. Search box, scrolling, byte usage bar. Shift-click moves stacks, right-click splits.

§eCrafting Terminal§r — a Terminal with a 3x3 crafting grid; ingredients are taken from the network.

§eWireless Terminal§r — see the Wireless Terminal chapter.

§eAny terminal§r: sort by name or count with the buttons on the right; dimmed items are craftable but out of stock — click to order. Ctrl + click (or middle click) orders a craft of an item in stock.
guide.simple_bytestorage.autocraft.title: Autocrafting
guide.simple_bytestorage.autocraft.body:
§eEncoding Terminal§r: choose the mode.
- §bCrafting§r: click items onto the 3x3 grid (not consumed); the vanilla recipe decides the result. Press Encode: the recipe goes straight into the network, no Pattern needed.
- §bProcessing§r: put a blank §bPattern§r in and set inputs and the result for furnaces and other machines; such patterns go into a Pattern Bus.

§ePattern Terminal§r: list of all patterns. Search, 'Ready' filter, a missing ingredient is shown. Order: LMB = 1, Shift = 10, Ctrl = 64. A window shows the full plan (sub-crafts included) before you confirm. The Queue tab shows running orders and lets you cancel them. Shift+LMB on × removes a pattern.

Ingredients that have their own pattern are crafted automatically (sub-crafts, depth up to 8).
guide.simple_bytestorage.assembler.title: Assembler
guide.simple_bytestorage.assembler.body:
Crafts crafting-table patterns. Put any §bstorage cell§r in as its buffer: the Assembler copies the ingredients into it, crafts, and returns results to the network.

§eSpeed cards§r: 4 upgrade slots. Time per craft = 40 / (1 + cards) ticks, minimum 4.

If it waits, the GUI shows why: no card, no resources, network offline/full.
guide.simple_bytestorage.provider.title: Pattern Bus
guide.simple_bytestorage.provider.body:
For machine crafts (furnace, smelter, and so on). Holds 9 processing patterns.

Place it §badjacent to the machine§r and connect it to the network. On an order it pushes the inputs into the machine and pulls finished products back from any side. Up to 16 jobs can be in flight; the queue is shown in the GUI.
guide.simple_bytestorage.iobus.title: I/O Bus
guide.simple_bytestorage.iobus.body:
Moves items between a neighbouring inventory and the network automatically.

- §bImport§r: pulls from the inventory into the network (filter: empty = everything).
- §bExport§r: keeps the listed items in the inventory; the count in a filter slot is the amount to keep.

Switch the mode with the button in the GUI.
guide.simple_bytestorage.jei.title: JEI integration
guide.simple_bytestorage.jei.body:
If JEI is installed, the '+' button in a recipe moves it into the Encoding Terminal:
- crafting recipe -> Crafting mode;
- furnace / smelter / smoker / stonecutter -> Processing mode (inputs + result).

JEI is optional; without it everything works as before.

gui.simple_bytestorage.wireless.list.tip: Whitelist: only listed items. Blacklist: everything except listed. Empty filter = everything.
guide.simple_bytestorage.controller.body:
Right-click the §eController§r to open its screen.
§bOverview§r: status, energy, buffer and drain, and which blocks are connected.
§bStorage§r: disk load bar, item types and the most plentiful items.
§bCrafting§r: patterns, busy Assemblers, Pattern Bus jobs and the current craft queue.
The slot at the bottom takes a §eWireless Terminal§r: it is bound to this network and charged from the controller automatically.
guide.simple_bytestorage.wireless.title: Wireless Terminal
guide.simple_bytestorage.wireless.body:
Opens the network from afar (right-click). Put it into the Controller's slot to §bbind§r and §bcharge§r it. 20 000 FE, an opening costs 100 FE; the controller chunk must be loaded.

§eUpgrades§r: Shift + right-click opens the settings. Install an §bAuto-Transfer Card§r (2 slots):
- §bRestock§r: the stack in your hand is refilled from the network.
- §bPickup§r: picked-up items go straight into the network.
- Filter (9 ghost slots) with Whitelist/Blacklist; an empty filter means everything.
Each moved item costs 2 FE of the terminal's energy.
